solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Play on words is hard to beat

parts.note: a play on words is a pun
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A remark that wordplay is very difficult to better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' at the end looks like part of 'hard to beat', but it is the definition, in the sense of thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone as a penalty is to discipline them physically, a synonym.

clue.text: Article supporting popular landlord

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so the article comes below

parts.note: public means of the people, popular
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article backs a well-liked landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord in Britain is called this, the keeper of a licensed house.

clue.text: Badly-written thing, notice in club

indicators.note: badly written suggests the letters of the word thing are scrambled

parts.note: to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: A poorly written thing is seen in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly-written' rearranges THING into NIGHT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is an entertainment venue open late, a place for evening outings.

clue.text: Short Greek island sausage that's highly-spiced

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the island's last letter is lost

parts.note: Salamis is a Greek island near Athens

explanation.surface: A brief description of a spicy sausage from a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the final S of SALAMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured, strongly seasoned Italian sausage, usually eaten sliced cold.

clue.text: Author in IOW resort dropping second name

indicators.note: dropping means removing, and second says it is the later of the two Ns in the resort's name that goes

parts.note: Ventnor is a seaside resort on the Isle of Wight (IOW)

explanation.surface: A writer is staying in a resort on the Isle of Wight and has stopped using a middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTNOR is a resort town on the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast. Losing its second N leaves VENTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An author in the broad sense is the originator or creator of something, as a deviser of new devices is.

clue.text: Those speaking more concisely do, naturally?

definitions.text: Those speaking more concisely do, naturally?

parts.words: Those speaking more concisely do, naturally?
parts.note: concise speakers cut out words that are not required, so they refrain from voicing the superfluous; the phrase also means 'obviously'

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'obviously', and cryptically describes what terse speakers leave out: unnecessary remarks.

clue.text: Insisted on precise editor

parts.note: exact means precise

explanation.surface: Someone demanded a meticulous editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand and obtain it, to require it insistently.

clue.text: Organised tour round duke's house

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for duke
organised suggests the letters of tour are arranged afresh

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A guided tour has been arranged around a nobleman's stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' turns TOUR into TUOR, which goes 'round' D. 'house' means royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A house can be a royal dynasty, and Henry VIII's family was the English one of this name.

clue.text: Hardly ever right, a bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely, to depend

explanation.surface: A river bank is almost never on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb, as in bank on, not a riverside or a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom, infrequently: both mean happening only on few occasions.

clue.text: British member back on a roll

indicators.note: back says the word for the limb is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A British club member is returning to a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEG into GEL; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked, is this item.

clue.text: Boy band leader?

definitions.meaning: Irving Berlin's song '... Ragtime Band' makes a man of this name the leader of a band

explanation.definitionFit: A common male forename, and the man whose ragtime band gives Berlin's song its title.

clue.text: The cartoonist sacked with little warning

indicators.note: sacked suggests the words are ransacked, thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: A newspaper fired its cartoonist without giving any notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with only a brief period of advance notice, almost at once.

clue.text: Narrow strip of land is like this over miles

indicators.note: over here means placed across, so the word for 'like this' straddles the abbreviation for miles

parts.note: thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A description of a long thin piece of land stretching for miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow neck of land joining two larger land masses, such as Panama, is the geographical term.

clue.text: Actual misprint

definitions.meaning: real, exact, taken in the strict sense
a printing error, a typo in a single character

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'exact, not figurative' and is also printers' jargon for a typographical error.

clue.text: A record on small and high mountains

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A record is being made on little peaks and big ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The great European mountain range spanning Switzerland, France, Italy and Austria.

clue.text: Judge in Tory party, first to resign

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, i.e. a Tory
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the following word, resign

explanation.surface: A judge in the Conservative party is the first to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something is to weigh it up or regard it in a particular way, a synonym.

clue.text: Strenghten check on behalf of church

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
for means on behalf of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Restraint exercised for the church's sake makes it stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something stronger, as by adding support or extra troops, is the meaning.

clue.text: Cover defending beautiful woman, defamed

indicators.note: defending means protecting, so the cover wraps around the beauty

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A cover story protecting a beauty who was slandered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be defamed in writing is the legal sense of the word, damaging a reputation falsely.

clue.text: Toddlers with it coming back awfully snotty

indicators.note: coming back says the two-letter word it is turned round
awfully suggests the following word is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Small children, already unpleasant, return being horribly snotty-nosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' gives TI; 'awfully' rearranges SNOTTY into NYTOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children just learning to walk are informally called this phrase.

clue.text: Small number at Russian river, as is to be expected

parts.note: N is the short form of number
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A handful of people at a Russian river, as one would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is normal and expected, the way things would usually go.

clue.text: Married in one, a short skirt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone got married wearing a single short skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the thigh-high skirt popularised in the 1960s.

clue.text: Scoundrel with gag

parts.note: to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: A villain armed with a joke, or with a mouth gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' is the verb meaning heave, not a joke or a mouth-stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a despicable person, a rogue or villain.

clue.text: Seconds — large cross-section

parts.note: ample means large, plentiful

explanation.surface: A food order: second helpings, and a big slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative selection drawn from a larger group, as in a survey.

clue.text: Rice dish recipe — it's too complicated

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take')

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the instructions for a rice meal are too involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock is this.

clue.text: Vision of number changing leader

indicators.note: changing leader means the first letter of the number is swapped for another

parts.note: eight is a number

explanation.surface: A view of a number that alters its first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing leader' swaps the E at the front of EIGHT for an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision and sight are synonyms for the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Appropriate bit

definitions.meaning: here a verb: to take for oneself, to pinch
a kind of mouthpiece for a horse's bridle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to steal informally, and is also a jointed bit for a horse.

clue.text: Wendy's last behind girl I let out and princess Peter Pan saved

indicators.note: behind places the final piece after the jumbled part
let out suggests the letters are released and jumbled into a different shape
last points to the end letter of Wendy

explanation.surface: A Peter Pan scene: Wendy trails the girl he frees, the princess he rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GIRL I LET into TIGERLIL, and Y, the end of Wendy, comes behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: In J. M. Barrie's story, Peter Pan rescues the Native American princess of this name from pirates.

clue.text: Beautiful fairy left in danger

parts.note: a peri is a beautiful fairy of Persian mythology

explanation.surface: A lovely fairy has been abandoned to her fate in a hazardous spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril and danger are direct synonyms for serious risk.

clue.text: Ritz, say, may offer more comfortable time for male

indicators.note: time for male means the letter for time takes the place of the letter for male

parts.note: homelier means cosier, more comfortable

explanation.surface: A posh London hotel promises cosier rooms, with time set aside for men.
explanation.walkthrough: César Ritz, founder of the Ritz hotels, is the example; 'say' marks him as one of a class.
explanation.definitionFit: César Ritz was a famous Swiss proprietor of luxury hotels, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Motto on one side of court

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
each half of a tennis court is an end, as players change ends

explanation.surface: A motto is displayed on one side of a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word, but in cricket the on side is the leg side, so it gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is an inscription or motto, as on a coin or coat of arms.
